learning_question: In a survivorship-free point-in-time US universe, does the frozen value screen's buy tier (buy + strong_buy) beat (a) the equal-weight universe and (b) a plain top-30% earnings-yield sort of the same names, on total return after costs?
universe: S&P 500 members on each rebalance date (Sharadar sp500 table), common stock, active and delisted. Financials and real estate included, as in the live screen; reported split by sector.

data_source.vendor: Sharadar personal-use licence (sharadar.com), Core US Equities Bundle, full history
data_source.fundamentals: fundamentals table, dimension ART (as-reported trailing twelve months), latest row with datekey (SEC filing date) at least 2 days before the rebalance date
data_source.prices: stocks table closeadj (split, dividend and spinoff adjusted) for total return; close (unadjusted) times sharesbas for market cap
data_source.licence_handling: Raw tables stay outside the repository and are deleted within 30 days of cancelling. Only cohort-level aggregates are committed.

rebalance.cadence: last trading day of each month

holdout.reveal_rule: Revealed once, after the development window is reviewed and nothing in this file has changed. Later reveals are exploratory.

primary.pass_bar: Holdout 90% interval on the primary metric lies wholly above zero, and the 365-day holdout net spread is not wholly below zero (the monthly edge does not reverse over a year).

comparators.universe: equal-weight return of every name with entry and exit prices
comparators.plain_value: equal-weight top 30% by positive earnings yield (earnings_yield_pe) among the same names

costs.model: net spread = gross buy-tier spread - 2 x cost x buy-tier turnover versus the entry one horizon earlier; the universe comparator is costless

delisting.rule: A name whose prices end before the exit date exits at its last adjusted close times (1 + haircut). Baseline 0; sensitivity -30% for delistings that were not mergers or acquisitions.

fixed_rules: No threshold, weight, or model search on any window (N33).
Model weights stay at defaults; the 28-day learner is not run (N197).
Per-model rank IC may be reported but never tunes the screen.
Any change to this file or to the fingerprinted screen code after the holdout is revealed opens a new registration_id; its results are exploratory.

decisions.pass_both: Buy tier beats the universe and the plain value sort: keep the screen's machinery; multi-year total return becomes the fitness test N197 asks for.
decisions.pass_universe_only: Beats the universe but not the plain sort: our extras add nothing over textbook value; simplify toward the published sorts.
decisions.fail_universe: Does not beat the universe: stop building forward machinery on this screen and rethink before stage 4.
